stage_description: The senior stage is 10+ years; the 2021 AAHA/AAFP update merged the former senior and super-senior stages into one. Chronic kidney disease, hyperthyroidism, hypertension, arthritis, and cognitive dysfunction become more common. For indoor cats this is usually the final third of a 12–18 year life. The goal of care is early disease detection, arthritis pain relief, and maintaining comfort.
nutrition: A senior diet with digestible, quality protein and kidney support where indicated. Monitor appetite and weight closely: subtle weight loss is a common early sign of disease. Adequate hydration is especially important.
activity: Gentle regular activity and mental stimulation within the cat's ability. Make resources accessible: low-sided litter boxes, steps to favorite spots, warm soft beds, and non-slip surfaces for arthritic joints.
veterinary_check_frequency: Exams every 6 months with expanded blood chemistry, urinalysis, blood-pressure measurement, and T4 (thyroid) testing to detect and manage age-related disease early.
dental_care: Regular dental assessment — periodontal disease and tooth-resorptive lesions are particularly common and painful at this stage. Cleaning is done weighing the older cat's anesthetic risk.
warning_signs: Increased thirst, weight loss, appetite changes, disorientation or night-time vocalizing (cognitive dysfunction), stiffness, and reduced grooming. Any of these warrants a veterinary evaluation.
disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and does not replace consultation with a veterinarian.
